readings.text: <v>1</v> “Surely the day is coming; it will burn like a furnace. All the arrogant and every evildoer will be stubble, and the day that is coming will set them on fire,” says the Lord Almighty. “Not a root or a branch will be left to them. <v>2</v> But for you who revere my name, the sun of righteousness will rise with healing in its rays. And you will go out and frolic like well-fed calves. <v>3</v> Then you will trample on the wicked; they will be ashes under the soles of your feet on the day when I act,” says the Lord Almighty. <v>4</v> “Remember the law of my servant Moses, the decrees and laws I gave him at Horeb for all Israel. <v>5</v> “See, I will send the prophet Elijah to you before that great and dreadful day of the Lord comes. <v>6</v> He will turn the hearts of the parents to their children, and the hearts of the children to their parents; or else I will come and strike the land with total destruction.”

<v>12</v> The next morning some Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves with an oath not to eat or drink until they had killed Paul. <v>13</v> More than forty men were involved in this plot. <v>14</v> They went to the chief priests and the elders and said, “We have taken a solemn oath not to eat anything until we have killed Paul. <v>15</v> Now then, you and the Sanhedrin petition the commander to bring him before you on the pretext of wanting more accurate information about his case. We are ready to kill him before he gets here.” <v>16</v> But when the son of Paul’s sister heard of this plot, he went into the barracks and told Paul. <v>17</v> Then Paul called one of the centurions and said, “Take this young man to the commander; he has something to tell him.” <v>18</v> So he took him to the commander. The centurion said, “Paul, the prisoner, sent for me and asked me to bring this young man to you because he has something to tell you.” <v>19</v> The commander took the young man by the hand, drew him aside and asked, “What is it you want to tell me?” <v>20</v> He said: “Some Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul before the Sanhedrin tomorrow on the pretext of wanting more accurate information about him. <v>21</v> Don’t give in to them, because more than forty of them are waiting in ambush for him. They have taken an oath not to eat or drink until they have killed him. They are ready now, waiting for your consent to their request.” <v>22</v> The commander dismissed the young man with this warning: “Don’t tell anyone that you have reported this to me.”

<v>5</v> In the time of Herod king of Judea there was a priest named Zechariah, who belonged to the priestly division of Abijah; his wife Elizabeth was also a descendant of Aaron. <v>6</v> Both of them were righteous in the sight of God, observing all the Lord’s commands and decrees blamelessly. <v>7</v> But they were childless because Elizabeth was not able to conceive, and they were both very old. <v>8</v> Once when Zechariah’s division was on duty and he was serving as priest before God, <v>9</v> he was chosen by lot, according to the custom of the priesthood, to go into the temple of the Lord and burn incense. <v>10</v> And when the time for the burning of incense came, all the assembled worshipers were praying outside. <v>11</v> Then an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing at the right side of the altar of incense. <v>12</v> When Zechariah saw him, he was startled and was gripped with fear. <v>13</v> But the angel said to him: “Do not be afraid, Zechariah; your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you are to call him John. <v>14</v> He will be a joy and delight to you, and many will rejoice because of his birth, <v>15</v> for he will be great in the sight of the Lord. He is never to take wine or other fermented drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even before he is born. <v>16</v> He will bring back many of the people of Israel to the Lord their God. <v>17</v> And he will go on before the Lord, in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the parents to their children and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous—to make ready a people prepared for the Lord.” <v>18</v> Zechariah asked the angel, “How can I be sure of this? I am an old man and my wife is well along in years.” <v>19</v> The angel said to him, “I am Gabriel. I stand in the presence of God, and I have been sent to speak to you and to tell you this good news. <v>20</v> And now you will be silent and not able to speak until the day this happens, because you did not believe my words, which will come true at their appointed time.” <v>21</v> Meanwhile, the people were waiting for Zechariah and wondering why he stayed so long in the temple. <v>22</v> When he came out, he could not speak to them. They realized he had seen a vision in the temple, for he kept making signs to them but remained unable to speak. <v>23</v> When his time of service was completed, he returned home. <v>24</v> After this his wife Elizabeth became pregnant and for five months remained in seclusion. <v>25</v> “The Lord has done this for me,” she said. “In these days he has shown his favor and taken away my disgrace among the people.”

<v>19</v> I hope in the Lord Jesus to send Timothy to you soon, that I also may be cheered when I receive news about you. <v>20</v> I have no one else like him, who will show genuine concern for your welfare. <v>21</v> For everyone looks out for their own interests, not those of Jesus Christ. <v>22</v> But you know that Timothy has proved himself, because as a son with his father he has served with me in the work of the gospel. <v>23</v> I hope, therefore, to send him as soon as I see how things go with me. <v>24</v> And I am confident in the Lord that I myself will come soon.

<v>25</v> On one occasion an expert in the law stood up to test Jesus. “Teacher,” he asked, “what must I do to inherit eternal life?” <v>26</v> <red>“What is written in the Law?”</red> he replied. <red>“How do you read it?”</red> <v>27</v> He answered, “ ‘Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind’; and, ‘Love your neighbor as yourself.’” <v>28</v> <red>“You have answered correctly,”</red> Jesus replied. <red>“Do this and you will live.”</red> <v>29</v> But he wanted to justify himself, so he asked Jesus, “And who is my neighbor?” <v>30</v> In reply Jesus said: <red>“A man was going down from Jerusalem to Jericho, when he was attacked by robbers. They stripped him of his clothes, beat him and went away, leaving him half dead.</red> <v>31</v> <red>A priest happened to be going down the same road, and when he saw the man, he passed by on the other side.</red> <v>32</v> <red>So too, a Levite, when he came to the place and saw him, passed by on the other side.</red> <v>33</v> <red>But a Samaritan, as he traveled, came where the man was; and when he saw him, he took pity on him.</red> <v>34</v> <red>He went to him and bandaged his wounds, pouring on oil and wine. Then he put the man on his own donkey, brought him to an inn and took care of him.</red> <v>35</v> <red>The next day he took out two denarii</red> <red>and gave them to the innkeeper. ‘Look after him,’ he said, ‘and when I return, I will reimburse you for any extra expense you may have.’</red> <v>36</v> <red>“Which of these three do you think was a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of robbers?”</red> <v>37</v> The expert in the law replied, “The one who had mercy on him.” Jesus told him, <red>“Go and do likewise.”</red>

<v>1</v> Praise the Lord. Sing to the Lord a new song, his praise in the assembly of his faithful people. <v>2</v> Let Israel rejoice in their Maker; let the people of Zion be glad in their King. <v>3</v> Let them praise his name with dancing and make music to him with timbrel and harp. <v>4</v> For the Lord takes delight in his people; he crowns the humble with victory. <v>5</v> Let his faithful people rejoice in this honor and sing for joy on their beds. <v>6</v> May the praise of God be in their mouths and a double-edged sword in their hands, <v>7</v> to inflict vengeance on the nations and punishment on the peoples, <v>8</v> to bind their kings with fetters, their nobles with shackles of iron, <v>9</v> to carry out the sentence written against them— this is the glory of all his faithful people. Praise the Lord.

<v>10</v> Concerning this salvation, the prophets, who spoke of the grace that was to come to you, searched intently and with the greatest care, <v>11</v> trying to find out the time and circumstances to which the Spirit of Christ in them was pointing when he predicted the sufferings of the Messiah and the glories that would follow. <v>12</v> It was revealed to them that they were not serving themselves but you, when they spoke of the things that have now been told you by those who have preached the gospel to you by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven. Even angels long to look into these things.

<v>21</v> At that time Jesus, full of joy through the Holy Spirit, said, <red>“I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and learned, and revealed them to little children. Yes, Father, for this is what you were pleased to do.</red> <v>22</v> <red>“All things have been committed to me by my Father. <v>21</v> When her husband Elkanah went up with all his family to offer the annual sacrifice to the Lord and to fulfill his vow, <v>22</v> Hannah did not go. She said to her husband, “After the boy is weaned, I will take him and present him before the Lord, and he will live there always.” <v>23</v> “Do what seems best to you,” her husband Elkanah told her. “Stay here until you have weaned him; only may the Lord make good his word.” So the woman stayed at home and nursed her son until she had weaned him. <v>24</v> After he was weaned, she took the boy with her, young as he was, along with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour and a skin of wine, and brought him to the house of the Lord at Shiloh. <v>25</v> When the bull had been sacrificed, they brought the boy to Eli, <v>26</v> and she said to him, “Pardon me, my lord. As surely as you live, I am the woman who stood here beside you praying to the Lord. <v>27</v> I prayed for this child, and the Lord has granted me what I asked of him. <v>28</v> So now I give him to the Lord. For his whole life he will be given over to the Lord.” And he worshiped the Lord there.

<v>1</v> What shall we say, then? Shall we go on sinning so that grace may increase? <v>2</v> By no means! We are those who have died to sin; how can we live in it any longer? <v>3</v> Or don’t you know that all of us who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? <v>4</v> We were therefore buried with him through baptism into death in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, we too may live a new life. <v>5</v> For if we have been united with him in a death like his, we will certainly also be united with him in a resurrection like his. <v>6</v> For we know that our old self was crucified with him so that the body ruled by sin might be done away with, that we should no longer be slaves to sin— <v>7</v> because anyone who has died has been set free from sin. <v>8</v> Now if we died with Christ, we believe that we will also live with him. <v>9</v> For we know that since Christ was raised from the dead, he cannot die again; death no longer has mastery over him. <v>10</v> The death he died, he died to sin once for all; but the life he lives, he lives to God. <v>11</v> In the same way, count yourselves dead to sin but alive to God in Christ Jesus.

Do not sow your fields or prune your vineyards. <v>5</v> Do not reap what grows of itself or harvest the grapes of your untended vines. The land is to have a year of rest.

<v>20</v> You may ask, “What will we eat in the seventh year if we do not plant or harvest our crops?” <v>21</v> I will send you such a blessing in the sixth year that the land will yield enough for three years. <v>22</v> While you plant during the eighth year, you will eat from the old crop and will continue to eat from it until the harvest of the ninth year comes in. <v>23</v> “ ‘The land must not be sold permanently, because the land is mine and you reside in my land as foreigners and strangers.

<v>15</v> The Son is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation. <v>16</v> For in him all things were created: things in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones or powers or rulers or authorities; all things have been created through him and for him. <v>17</v> He is before all things, and in him all things hold together. <v>18</v> And he is the head of the body, the church; he is the beginning and the firstborn from among the dead, so that in everything he might have the supremacy.

<v>22</v> Then Jesus said to his disciples: <red>“Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat; or about your body, what you will wear.</red> <v>23</v> <red>For life is more than food, and the body more than clothes.</red> <v>24</v> <red>Consider the ravens: They do not sow or reap, they have no storeroom or barn; yet God feeds them. And how much more valuable you are than birds!</red> <v>25</v> <red>Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to your life</red><red>?</red> <v>26</v> <red>Since you cannot do this very little thing, why do you worry about the rest?</red> <v>27</v> <red>“Consider how the wild flowers grow. They do not labor or spin. Yet I tell you, not even Solomon in all his splendor was dressed like one of these.</red>

<v>11</v> For you this whole vision is nothing but words sealed in a scroll. And if you give the scroll to someone who can read, and say, “Read this, please,” they will answer, “I can’t; it is sealed.” <v>12</v> Or if you give the scroll to someone who cannot read, and say, “Read this, please,” they will answer, “I don’t know how to read.” <v>13</v> The Lord says: “These people come near to me with their mouth and honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me. Their worship of me is based on merely human rules they have been taught. <v>14</v> Therefore once more I will astound these people with wonder upon wonder; the wisdom of the wise will perish, the intelligence of the intelligent will vanish.” <v>15</v> Woe to those who go to great depths to hide their plans from the Lord, who do their work in darkness and think, “Who sees us? Who will know?” <v>16</v> You turn things upside down, as if the potter were thought to be like the clay! Shall what is formed say to the one who formed it, “You did not make me”? Can the pot say to the potter, “You know nothing”? <v>17</v> In a very short time, will not Lebanon be turned into a fertile field and the fertile field seem like a forest? <v>18</v> In that day the deaf will hear the words of the scroll, and out of gloom and darkness the eyes of the blind will see.

<v>16</v> Therefore do not let anyone judge you by what you eat or drink, or with regard to a religious festival, a New Moon celebration or a Sabbath day. <v>17</v> These are a shadow of the things that were to come; the reality, however, is found in Christ. <v>18</v> Do not let anyone who delights in false humility and the worship of angels disqualify you. Such a person also goes into great detail about what they have seen; they are puffed up with idle notions by their unspiritual mind. <v>19</v> They have lost connection with the head, from whom the whole body, supported and held together by its ligaments and sinews, grows as God causes it to grow. <v>20</v> Since you died with Christ to the elemental spiritual forces of this world, why, as though you still belonged to the world, do you submit to its rules: <v>21</v> “Do not handle! Do not taste! Do not touch!”? <v>22</v> These rules, which have to do with things that are all destined to perish with use, are based on merely human commands and teachings. <v>23</v> Such regulations indeed have an appearance of wisdom, with their self-imposed worship, their false humility and their harsh treatment of the body, but they lack any value in restraining sensual indulgence.

<v>1</v> The Pharisees and some of the teachers of the law who had come from Jerusalem gathered around Jesus <v>2</v> and saw some of his disciples eating food with hands that were defiled, that is, unwashed. <v>3</v> (The Pharisees and all the Jews do not eat unless they give their hands a ceremonial washing, holding to the tradition of the elders. <v>4</v> When they come from the marketplace they do not eat unless they wash. And they observe many other traditions, such as the washing of cups, pitchers and kettles.) <v>5</v> So the Pharisees and teachers of the law asked Jesus, “Why don’t your disciples live according to the tradition of the elders instead of eating their food with defiled hands?” <v>6</v> He replied, <red>“Isaiah was right when he prophesied about you hypocrites; as it is written:</red> <red>“ ‘These people honor me with their lips,</red> <red>but their hearts are far from me.</red> <v>7</v> <red>They worship me in vain;</red> <red>their teachings are merely human rules.’</red> <v>8</v> <red>You have let go of the commands of God and are holding on to human traditions.”</red> <v>9</v> And he continued, <red>“You have a fine way of setting aside the commands of God in order to observe</red> <red>your own traditions!</red> <v>10</v> <red>For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and mother,’</red> <red>and, ‘Anyone who curses their father or mother is to be put to death.’</red> <v>11</v> <red>But you say that if anyone declares that what might have been used to help their father or mother is Corban (that is, devoted to God)—</red> <v>12</v> <red>then you no longer let them do anything for their father or mother.</red> <v>13</v> <red>Thus you nullify the word of God by your tradition that you have handed down. And you do many things like that.”</red>

<v>1</v> Why, Lord, do you stand far off? Why do you hide yourself in times of trouble? <v>2</v> In his arrogance the wicked man hunts down the weak, who are caught in the schemes he devises. <v>3</v> He boasts about the cravings of his heart; he blesses the greedy and reviles the Lord. <v>4</v> In his pride the wicked man does not seek him; in all his thoughts there is no room for God. <v>5</v> His ways are always prosperous; your laws are rejected by him; he sneers at all his enemies. <v>6</v> He says to himself, “Nothing will ever shake me.” He swears, “No one will ever do me harm.” <v>7</v> His mouth is full of lies and threats; trouble and evil are under his tongue. <v>8</v> He lies in wait near the villages; from ambush he murders the innocent. His eyes watch in secret for his victims; <v>9</v> like a lion in cover he lies in wait. He lies in wait to catch the helpless; he catches the helpless and drags them off in his net. <v>10</v> His victims are crushed, they collapse; they fall under his strength.

<v>7</v> Dear friends, I am not writing you a new command but an old one, which you have had since the beginning. This old command is the message you have heard. <v>8</v> Yet I am writing you a new command; its truth is seen in him and in you, because the darkness is passing and the true light is already shining. <v>9</v> Anyone who claims to be in the light but hates a brother or sister is still in the darkness. <v>10</v> Anyone who loves their brother and sister lives in the light, and there is nothing in them to make them stumble. <v>11</v> But anyone who hates a brother or sister is in the darkness and walks around in the darkness. They do not know where they are going, because the darkness has blinded them. <v>12</v> I am writing to you, dear children, because your sins have been forgiven on account of his name. <v>13</v> I am writing to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. I am writing to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. <v>14</v> I write to you, dear children, because you know the Father. I write to you, fathers, because you know him who is from the beginning. <v>34</v> “Who has known the mind of the Lord? Or who has been his counselor?” <v>35</v> “Who has ever given to God, that God should repay them?”
<v>31</v> The one who comes from above is above all; the one who is from the earth belongs to the earth, and speaks as one from the earth. The one who comes from heaven is above all.

<v>2</v> Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth— for your love is more delightful than wine. <v>3</v> Pleasing is the fragrance of your perfumes; your name is like perfume poured out. <v>1</v> Now the Festival of Unleavened Bread, called the Passover, was approaching, <v>2</v> and the chief priests and the teachers of the law were looking for some way to get rid of Jesus, for they were afraid of the people. <v>3</v> Then Satan entered Judas, called Iscariot, one of the Twelve. <v>4</v> And Judas went to the chief priests and the officers of the temple guard and discussed with them how he might betray Jesus. <v>5</v> They were delighted and agreed to give him money. <v>6</v> He consented, and watched for an opportunity to hand Jesus over to them when no crowd was present. <v>7</v> Then came the day of Unleavened Bread on which the Passover lamb had to be sacrificed. <v>8</v> Jesus sent Peter and John, saying, <red>“Go and make preparations for us to eat the Passover.”</red> <v>9</v> “Where do you want us to prepare for it?” they asked. <v>10</v> He replied, <red>“As you enter the city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him to the house that he enters,</red> <v>11</v> <red>and say to the owner of the house, ‘The Teacher asks: Where is the guest room, where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’</red> <v>12</v> <red>He will show you a large room upstairs, all furnished. <v>1</v> “Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen one in whom I delight; I will put my Spirit on him, and he will bring justice to the nations. <v>2</v> He will not shout or cry out, or raise his voice in the streets. <v>3</v> A bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not snuff out. In his teaching the islands will put their hope.” <v>5</v> This is what God the Lord says— the Creator of the heavens, who stretches them out, who spreads out the earth with all that springs from it, who gives breath to its people, and life to those who walk on it: <v>6</v> “I, the Lord, have called you in righteousness; I will take hold of your hand. <v>51</v> “You stiff-necked people! Your hearts and ears are still uncircumcised. <v>39</v> Jesus went out as usual to the Mount of Olives, and his disciples followed him. <v>40</v> On reaching the place, he said to them, <red>“Pray that you will not fall into temptation.”</red> <v>41</v> He withdrew about a stone’s throw beyond them, knelt down and prayed, <v>42</v> <red>“Father, if you are willing, take this cup from me; yet not my will, but yours be done.”</red> <v>43</v> An angel from heaven appeared to him and strengthened him. <v>44</v> And being in anguish, he prayed more earnestly, and his sweat was like drops of blood falling to the ground. <v>45</v> When he rose from prayer and went back to the disciples, he found them asleep, exhausted from sorrow. <v>46</v> <red>“Why are you sleeping?”</red> he asked them. <red>“Get up and pray so that you will not fall into temptation.”</red>

<v>1</v> Listen to me, you islands; hear this, you distant nations: Before I was born the Lord called me; from my mother’s womb he has spoken my name. <v>2</v> He made my mouth like a sharpened sword, in the shadow of his hand he hid me; he made me into a polished arrow and concealed me in his quiver. <v>3</v> He said to me, “You are my servant, Israel, in whom I will display my splendor.” <v>4</v> But I said, “I have labored in vain; I have spent my strength for nothing at all. Yet what is due me is in the Lord’s hand, and my reward is with my God.” <v>5</v> And now the Lord says— he who formed me in the womb to be his servant to bring Jacob back to him and gather Israel to himself, for I am honored in the eyes of the Lord and my God has been my strength— <v>6</v> he says: “It is too small a thing for you to be my servant to restore the tribes of Jacob and bring back those of Israel I have kept. I will also make you a light for the Gentiles, that my salvation may reach to the ends of the earth.”

<v>1</v> Therefore if you have any encouragement from being united with Christ, if any comfort from his love, if any common sharing in the Spirit, if any tenderness and compassion, <v>2</v> then make my joy complete by being like-minded, having the same love, being one in spirit and of one mind. <v>3</v> Do nothing out of selfish ambition or vain conceit. <v>47</v> While he was still speaking a crowd came up, and the man who was called Judas, one of the Twelve, was leading them. But this is your hour—when darkness reigns.”</red>

<v>4</v> The Sovereign Lord has given me a well-instructed tongue, to know the word that sustains the weary. He wakens me morning by morning, wakens my ear to listen like one being instructed. <v>5</v> The Sovereign Lord has opened my ears; I have not been rebellious, I have not turned away. <v>6</v> I offered my back to those who beat me, my cheeks to those who pulled out my beard; I did not hide my face from mocking and spitting. <v>7</v> Because the Sovereign Lord helps me, I will not be disgraced. Therefore have I set my face like flint, and I know I will not be put to shame. <v>8</v> He who vindicates me is near. Who then will bring charges against me? Let us face each other! Who is my accuser? Let him confront me! <v>9</v> It is the Sovereign Lord who helps me. Who will condemn me? They will all wear out like a garment; the moths will eat them up.

<v>1</v> Then I looked, and there before me was the Lamb, standing on Mount Zion, and with him 144,000 who had his name and his Father’s name written on their foreheads. <v>2</v> And I heard a sound from heaven like the roar of rushing waters and like a loud peal of thunder. The sound I heard was like that of harpists playing their harps. <v>3</v> And they sang a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders. No one could learn the song except the 144,000 who had been redeemed from the earth. <v>4</v> These are those who did not defile themselves with women, for they remained virgins. They follow the Lamb wherever he goes. They were purchased from among mankind and offered as firstfruits to God and the Lamb. <v>5</v> No lie was found in their mouths; they are blameless.

<v>54</v> Then seizing him, they led him away and took him into the house of the high priest. Peter followed at a distance. <v>55</v> And when some there had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard and had sat down together, Peter sat down with them. <v>56</v> A servant girl saw him seated there in the firelight. She looked closely at him and said, “This man was with him.” <v>57</v> But he denied it. “Woman, I don’t know him,” he said. <v>58</v> A little later someone else saw him and said, “You also are one of them.” “Man, I am not!” Peter replied. <v>59</v> About an hour later another asserted, “Certainly this fellow was with him, for he is a Galilean.” <v>60</v> Peter replied, “Man, I don’t know what you’re talking about!” Just as he was speaking, the rooster crowed. <v>61</v> The Lord turned and looked straight at Peter. Then Peter remembered the word the Lord had spoken to him: <red>“Before the rooster crows today, you will disown me three times.”</red> <v>62</v> And he went outside and wept bitterly. <v>63</v> The men who were guarding Jesus began mocking and beating him. <v>64</v> They blindfolded him and demanded, “Prophesy! Who hit you?” <v>65</v> And they said many other insulting things to him. <v>66</v> At daybreak the council of the elders of the people, both the chief priests and the teachers of the law, met together, and Jesus was led before them. <v>67</v> “If you are the Messiah,” they said, “tell us.” Jesus answered, <red>“If I tell you, you will not believe me,</red> <v>68</v> <red>and if I asked you, you would not answer.</red> <v>69</v> <red>But from now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the mighty God.”</red> <v>70</v> They all asked, “Are you then the Son of God?” He replied, <red>“You say that I am.”</red> <v>71</v> Then they said, “Why do we need any more testimony? We have heard it from his own lips.”

<v>21</v> Then Moses summoned all the elders of Israel and said to them, “Go at once and select the animals for your families and slaughter the Passover lamb. <v>22</v> Take a bunch of hyssop, dip it into the blood in the basin and put some of the blood on the top and on both sides of the doorframe. None of you shall go out of the door of your house until morning. <v>23</v> When the Lord goes through the land to strike down the Egyptians, he will see the blood on the top and sides of the doorframe and will pass over that doorway, and he will not permit the destroyer to enter your houses and strike you down. <v>24</v> “Obey these instructions as a lasting ordinance for you and your descendants. <v>25</v> When you enter the land that the Lord will give you as he promised, observe this ceremony. <v>26</v> And when your children ask you, ‘What does this ceremony mean to you?’ <v>27</v> then tell them, ‘It is the Passover sacrifice to the Lord, who passed over the houses of the Israelites in Egypt and spared our homes when he struck down the Egyptians.’ ” Then the people bowed down and worshiped. <v>28</v> The Israelites did just what the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron.

<v>20</v> So then, when you come together, it is not the Lord’s Supper you eat, <v>21</v> for when you are eating, some of you go ahead with your own private suppers. As a result, one person remains hungry and another gets drunk. <v>22</v> Don’t you have homes to eat and drink in? Or do you despise the church of God by humiliating those who have nothing? What shall I say to you? Shall I praise you? Certainly not in this matter! <v>23</v> For I received from the Lord what I also passed on to you: The Lord Jesus, on the night he was betrayed, took bread, <v>24</v> and when he had given thanks, he broke it and said, <red>“This is my body, which is for you; do this in remembrance of me.”</red> <v>25</v> In the same way, after supper he took the cup, saying, <red>“This cup is the new covenant in my blood; do this, whenever you drink it, in remembrance of me.”</red> <v>26</v> For whenever you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes. <v>27</v> So then, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of sinning against the body and blood of the Lord. <v>28</v> Everyone ought to examine themselves before they eat of the bread and drink from the cup. <v>29</v> For those who eat and drink without discerning the body of Christ eat and drink judgment on themselves. <v>30</v> That is why many among you are weak and sick, and a number of you have fallen asleep. <v>31</v> But if we were more discerning with regard to ourselves, we would not come under such judgment. <v>32</v> Nevertheless, when we are judged in this way by the Lord, we are being disciplined so that we will not be finally condemned with the world.

<v>14</v> When the hour came, Jesus and his apostles reclined at the table. <v>15</v> And he said to them, <red>“I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer.</red> <v>16</v> <red>For I tell you, I will not eat it again until it finds fulfillment in the kingdom of God.”</red> <v>17</v> After taking the cup, he gave thanks and said, <red>“Take this and divide it among you.</red> <v>18</v> <red>For I tell you I will not drink again from the fruit of the vine until the kingdom of God comes.”</red> <v>19</v> And he took bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, <red>“This is my body given for you; do this in remembrance of me.”</red> <v>20</v> In the same way, after the supper he took the cup, saying, <red>“This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you.</red> <v>21</v> <red>But the hand of him who is going to betray me is with mine on the table.</red> <v>22</v> <red>The Son of Man will go as it has been decreed. But woe to that man who betrays him!”</red> <v>23</v> They began to question among themselves which of them it might be who would do this.

<v>12</v> Many bulls surround me; strong bulls of Bashan encircle me. <v>13</v> Roaring lions that tear their prey open their mouths wide against me. <v>14</v> I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint. My heart has turned to wax; it has melted within me. <v>15</v> My mouth is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue sticks to the roof of my mouth; you lay me in the dust of death. <v>16</v> Dogs surround me, a pack of villains encircles me; they pierce my hands and my feet. <v>17</v> All my bones are on display; people stare and gloat over me. <v>18</v> They divide my clothes among them and cast lots for my garment. <v>19</v> But you, Lord, do not be far from me. You are my strength; come quickly to help me. <v>20</v> Deliver me from the sword, my precious life from the power of the dogs. <v>21</v> Rescue me from the mouth of the lions; save me from the horns of the wild oxen.

<v>11</v> Therefore, remember that formerly you who are Gentiles by birth and called “uncircumcised” by those who call themselves “the circumcision” (which is done in the body by human hands)— <v>12</v> remember that at that time you were separate from Christ, excluded from citizenship in Israel and foreigners to the covenants of the promise, without hope and without God in the world. <v>13</v> But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far away have been brought near by the blood of Christ. <v>14</v> For he himself is our peace, who has made the two groups one and has destroyed the barrier, the dividing wall of hostility, <v>15</v> by setting aside in his flesh the law with its commands and regulations. His purpose was to create in himself one new humanity out of the two, thus making peace, <v>16</v> and in one body to reconcile both of them to God through the cross, by which he put to death their hostility.

<v>26</v> As the soldiers led him away, they seized Simon from Cyrene, who was on his way in from the country, and put the cross on him and made him carry it behind Jesus. <v>27</v> A large number of people followed him, including women who mourned and wailed for him. <v>28</v> Jesus turned and said to them, <red>“Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me; weep for yourselves and for your children.</red> <v>29</v> <red>For the time will come when you will say, ‘Blessed are the childless women, the wombs that never bore and the breasts that never nursed!’</red> <v>30</v> <red>Then</red> <red>“ ‘they will say to the mountains, “Fall on us!”</red> <red>and to the hills, “Cover us!” ’</red> <v>31</v> <red>For if people do these things when the tree is green, what will happen when it is dry?”</red> <v>32</v> Two other men, both criminals, were also led out with him to be executed. <v>33</v> When they came to the place called the Skull, they crucified him there, along with the criminals—one on his right, the other on his left. <v>34</v> Jesus said, <red>“Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.”</red> And they divided up his clothes by casting lots. <v>35</v> The people stood watching, and the rulers even sneered at him. They said, “He saved others; let him save himself if he is God’s Messiah, the Chosen One.” <v>36</v> The soldiers also came up and mocked him. They offered him wine vinegar <v>37</v> and said, “If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself.” <v>38</v> There was a written notice above him, which read: this is the king of the jews. <v>39</v> One of the criminals who hung there hurled insults at him: “Aren’t you the Messiah? Save yourself and us!” <v>40</v> But the other criminal rebuked him. “Don’t you fear God,” he said, “since you are under the same sentence? <v>41</v> We are punished justly, for we are getting what our deeds deserve. But this man has done nothing wrong.” <v>42</v> Then he said, “Jesus, remember me when you come into your kingdom.” <v>43</v> Jesus answered him, <red>“Truly I tell you, today you will be with me in paradise.”</red> <v>44</v> It was now about noon, and darkness came over the whole land until three in the afternoon, <v>45</v> for the sun stopped shining. And the curtain of the temple was torn in two. <v>46</v> Jesus called out with a loud voice, <red>“Father, into your hands I commit my spirit.”</red> When he had said this, he breathed his last. <v>47</v> The centurion, seeing what had happened, praised God and said, “Surely this was a righteous man.” <v>48</v> When all the people who had gathered to witness this sight saw what took place, they beat their breasts and went away. <v>49</v> But all those who knew him, including the women who had followed him from Galilee, stood at a distance, watching these things.

<v>5</v> Lord, you alone are my portion and my cup; you make my lot secure. <v>6</v> The boundary lines have fallen for me in pleasant places; surely I have a delightful inheritance. <v>7</v> I will praise the Lord, who counsels me; even at night my heart instructs me. <v>8</v> I keep my eyes always on the Lord. With him at my right hand, I will not be shaken. <v>9</v> Therefore my heart is glad and my tongue rejoices; my body also will rest secure, <v>10</v> because you will not abandon me to the realm of the dead, nor will you let your faithful one see decay. <v>11</v> You make known to me the path of life; you will fill me with joy in your presence, with eternal pleasures at your right hand.

<v>18</v> For Christ also suffered once for sins, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive in the Spirit. <v>19</v> After being made alive, he went and made proclamation to the imprisoned spirits— <v>20</v> to those who were disobedient long ago when God waited patiently in the days of Noah while the ark was being built. In it only a few people, eight in all, were saved through water,

<v>50</v> Now there was a man named Joseph, a member of the Council, a good and upright man, <v>51</v> who had not consented to their decision and action. He came from the Judean town of Arimathea, and he himself was waiting for the kingdom of God. <v>52</v> Going to Pilate, he asked for Jesus’ body. <v>53</v> Then he took it down, wrapped it in linen cloth and placed it in a tomb cut in the rock, one in which no one had yet been laid. <v>54</v> It was Preparation Day, and the Sabbath was about to begin. <v>55</v> The women who had come with Jesus from Galilee followed Joseph and saw the tomb and how his body was laid in it. <v>56</v> Then they went home and prepared spices and perfumes. But they rested on the Sabbath in obedience to the commandment.

<v>18</v> We were with child, we writhed in labor, but we gave birth to wind. We have not brought salvation to the earth, and the people of the world have not come to life. <v>19</v> But your dead will live, Lord; their bodies will rise— let those who dwell in the dust wake up and shout for joy— your dew is like the dew of the morning; the earth will give birth to her dead.

<v>15</v> For this reason, ever since I heard about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all God’s people, <v>16</v> I have not stopped giving thanks for you, remembering you in my prayers. <v>17</v> I keep asking that the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the glorious Father, may give you the Spirit of wisdom and revelation, so that you may know him better. <v>18</v> I pray that the eyes of your heart may be enlightened in order that you may know the hope to which he has called you, the riches of his glorious inheritance in his holy people, <v>19</v> and his incomparably great power for us who believe. That power is the same as the mighty strength <v>20</v> he exerted when he raised Christ from the dead and seated him at his right hand in the heavenly realms, <v>21</v> far above all rule and authority, power and dominion, and every name that is invoked, not only in the present age but also in the one to come. <v>22</v> And God placed all things under his feet and appointed him to be head over everything for the church, <v>23</v> which is his body, the fullness of him who fills everything in every way.

<v>1</v> On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, the women took the spices they had prepared and went to the tomb. <v>2</v> They found the stone rolled away from the tomb, <v>3</v> but when they entered, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus. <v>4</v> While they were wondering about this, suddenly two men in clothes that gleamed like lightning stood beside them. <v>5</v> In their fright the women bowed down with their faces to the ground, but the men said to them, “Why do you look for the living among the dead? <v>6</v> He is not here; he has risen! Remember how he told you, while he was still with you in Galilee: <v>7</v> <red>‘The Son of Man must be delivered over to the hands of sinners, be crucified and on the third day be raised again.’</red> ” <v>8</v> Then they remembered his words. <v>9</v> When they came back from the tomb, they told all these things to the Eleven and to all the others. <v>10</v> It was Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James, and the others with them who told this to the apostles. <v>11</v> But they did not believe the women, because their words seemed to them like nonsense. <v>12</v> Peter, however, got up and ran to the tomb. Bending over, he saw the strips of linen lying by themselves, and he went away, wondering to himself what had happened.

<v>9</v> They will come with weeping; they will pray as I bring them back. I will lead them beside streams of water on a level path where they will not stumble, because I am Israel’s father, and Ephraim is my firstborn son. <v>10</v> “Hear the word of the Lord, you nations; proclaim it in distant coastlands: ‘He who scattered Israel will gather them and will watch over his flock like a shepherd.’ <v>11</v> For the Lord will deliver Jacob and redeem them from the hand of those stronger than they.

<v>14</v> For Christ’s love compels us, because we are convinced that one died for all, and therefore all died. <v>15</v> And he died for all, that those who live should no longer live for themselves but for him who died for them and was raised again. <v>16</v> So from now on we regard no one from a worldly point of view. Though we once regarded Christ in this way, we do so no longer. <v>17</v> Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, the new creation has come: The old has gone, the new is here! <v>18</v> All this is from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ and gave us the ministry of reconciliation: <v>19</v> that God was reconciling the world to himself in Christ, not counting people’s sins against them. And he has committed to us the message of reconciliation. <v>20</v> We are therefore Christ’s ambassadors, as though God were making his appeal through us. We implore you on Christ’s behalf: Be reconciled to God. <v>21</v> God made him who had no sin to be sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.

You will lend to many nations but will borrow from none. <v>13</v> The Lord will make you the head, not the tail. If you pay attention to the commands of the Lord your God that I give you this day and carefully follow them, you will always be at the top, never at the bottom. <v>14</v> Do not turn aside from any of the commands I give you today, to the right or to the left, following other gods and serving them.

<v>12</v> Therefore, since we have such a hope, we are very bold. <v>13</v> We are not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face to prevent the Israelites from seeing the end of what was passing away. <v>14</v> But their minds were made dull, for to this day the same veil remains when the old covenant is read. It has not been removed, because only in Christ is it taken away. <v>15</v> Even to this day when Moses is read, a veil covers their hearts. <v>16</v> But whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away. <v>17</v> Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom. <v>18</v> And we all, who with unveiled faces contemplate the Lord’s glory, are being transformed into his image with ever-increasing glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.

<v>2</v> Hear me, you heavens! Listen, earth! For the Lord has spoken: “I reared children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against me. <v>3</v> The ox knows its master, the donkey its owner’s manger, but Israel does not know, my people do not understand.” <v>4</v> Woe to the sinful nation, a people whose guilt is great, a brood of evildoers, children given to corruption! They have forsaken the Lord; they have spurned the Holy One of Israel and turned their backs on him. <v>5</v> Why should you be beaten anymore? Why do you persist in rebellion? Your whole head is injured, your whole heart afflicted. <v>6</v> From the sole of your foot to the top of your head there is no soundness— only wounds and welts and open sores, not cleansed or bandaged or soothed with olive oil. <v>7</v> Your country is desolate, your cities burned with fire; your fields are being stripped by foreigners right before you, laid waste as when overthrown by strangers. <v>8</v> Daughter Zion is left like a shelter in a vineyard, like a hut in a cucumber field, like a city under siege. <v>9</v> Unless the Lord Almighty had left us some survivors, we would have become like Sodom, we would have been like Gomorrah.

<v>1</v> You foolish Galatians! Who has bewitched you? Before your very eyes Jesus Christ was clearly portrayed as crucified. <v>2</v> I would like to learn just one thing from you: Did you receive the Spirit by the works of the law, or by believing what you heard? <v>3</v> Are you so foolish? After beginning by means of the Spirit, are you now trying to finish by means of the flesh? <v>4</v> Have you experienced so much in vain—if it really was in vain? <v>5</v> So again I ask, does God give you his Spirit and work miracles among you by the works of the law, or by your believing what you heard? <v>6</v> So also Abraham “believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.” <v>7</v> Understand, then, that those who have faith are children of Abraham. <v>8</v> Scripture foresaw that God would justify the Gentiles by faith, and announced the gospel in advance to Abraham: “All nations will be blessed through you.” <v>9</v> So those who rely on faith are blessed along with Abraham, the man of faith.
